While critics have dismissed the Club World Cup as almost like a friendly tournament, that is not how it has been played. It is being taken as seriously as any competition by the players. 

Last month, senior officials from FIFA explained to BBC Sport that player welfare has been central to their decision-making process, highlighting measures like extra substitutes and permanent concussion substitutions as evidence of their commitment to this issue.

Prior to this, the leading European leagues and the players' union, Fifpro, lodged a legal complaint with the European Commission against Fifa, alleging what they describe as an "abuse of dominance" by the governing body of world football.
